sections.title: Bank Scale & Funding
sections.subtitle: Deposits, loan book and net interest income — the balance-sheet drivers a bank's DCF is built on

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Macquarie Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Macquarie Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS (diluted) is net income per share after dilutive MEREP awards; Basic EPS uses the actual weighted-average share count with no dilution adjustment. Both are in AUD major units.

For Macquarie Group Limited: the gap between basic and diluted EPS tracks unvested MEREP (staff equity scheme) awards; a widening gap signals rising future dilution even while the company buys back MEREP treasury shares to offset it.

What to watch:

  • Basic vs diluted EPS spread widening
  • EPS growth versus net income growth
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

loansDeposits.title: Net loans and deposits
loansDeposits.content:
Net loans is the loan book after provisions for credit losses; deposits are customer deposits funding that book, both measured at the balance-sheet date.

For Macquarie Group Limited: these are Banking and Financial Services' core balance-sheet scale metrics — loan and deposit growth drive net interest income more directly than the group's asset-management and markets-facing revenue lines, which dominate the headline Revenue chart above.

What to watch:

  • Deposits growing at least as fast as loans (funding self-sufficiency, avoids wholesale funding reliance)
  • Loan growth outpacing system growth (market share gain, but also potential risk appetite increase)

nii.title: Net interest income
nii.content:
Net interest income is interest earned on loans and other assets less interest paid on deposits and wholesale funding — the spread income of the banking business.

For Macquarie Group Limited: NII is only one slice of group revenue (Macquarie Asset Management and Macquarie Capital contribute fee and markets income that swing much more with market conditions), so NII growth should be read against loan-book growth, not against total group revenue growth.

What to watch:

  • NII growth versus net loan growth (margin compression or expansion)
  • Sensitivity to RBA rate moves given the deposit/loan mix

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Macquarie Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Macquarie Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Macquarie Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Macquarie Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Macquarie Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks; MEREP treasury share purchases is cash spent buying shares on-market to satisfy staff equity awards under the Macquarie Employee Retained Equity Plan.

For Macquarie Group Limited: MEREP purchases fund remuneration, not capital return -- a separate cash use from any on-market buyback the board runs for capital management, so do not read this line as shareholder-friendly buyback activity.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while MEREP purchases are advertised as offsetting dilution
  • SBC and MEREP purchases as a percentage of revenue
